messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: issues with truncated distributions
parts:
Many of the CDFs we just released have a bug relating
to the boundary behavior when given constants rather
than variables to evaluate.

This will affect truncated distributions that have
constant (i.e., not a parameter, transformed parameter
or local model variable) values.

For efficiency sake, you should NOT be truncating with respect
to constant truncation points in Stan. Just define the
variate in question to be bounded. So rather than this:

parameters {
real y;
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1) T[-1,1];
}

for a unit normal truncated to [-1,1], use this:

parameters {
real<lower=-1,upper=1> y;
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
}

Having said that, we need to fix this bug.
For the dev team, here's an example of the issue in
neg_binomial CDF:

// Return if everything is constant and only proportionality is required
if (!include_summand<propto,T_shape,T_inv_scale>::value)
return 0.0;

Because the CDFs are on the linear scale, not a log
scale, this should be returning 1.0, not 0.0.

- Bob
